==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|id=physical|:inh|enm:sporten<ety:from<enm:disporten<id:relax>>>|tree=1}}

From {{inh|en|enm|sporten|t=to divert, disport|pos=verb}} and {{m|enm|sport}}, {{m|enm|spoort}}, {{m|enm|sporte|pos=noun}}, apheretic shortenings of {{m|enm|disporten|pos=verb}} and {{m|enm|disport}}, {{m|enm|disporte|pos=noun}}, from {{der|en|fro|desporter|t=to divert, amuse, please, play; to seek amusement}}, etymologically meaning "to carry away (the mind from serious matters)," from {{pre|fro|des-|porter|nocat=1}}, from {{der|en|la|dis-}} + {{der|en|la|portāre}}, ultimately from {{der|en|la|deportāre}}, from {{pre|la|de-|portāre|nocat=1}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*per-|id=fare|t=to lead, pass over}}). Replaced native {{ncog|en|laik}}, {{m|en|lake|t=sport, fun, amusement}}, and {{ncog|enm|spile}}, {{m|enm|spyl|t=fun, sport, play}}. More at {{m|en|disport}}. {{doublet|en|disport|deport}}.

* {{rhymes|en|ɔː(ɹ)t|s=1}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{senseid|en|Q349}}{{lb|en|countable|uncountable}} Any activity that uses physical exertion or skills [[competitively]] under a set of rules that is not based on aesthetics.
#: {{ux|en|Basketball is her favorite '''sport''', and she also enjoys various other '''sports''' as well.}}<!--countable-->
#: {{ux|en|'''Sport''' can be an excellent form of exercise because the competition and sense of achievement can help with both motivation and pleasure.}}<!--uncountable-->
# {{lb|en|countable}} A person who exhibits either good or bad [[sportsmanship]].
#: {{ux|en|Jen may have won, but she was sure a poor '''sport'''; she laughed at the loser.}}
#: {{ux|en|The loser was a good '''sport''', and congratulated Jen on her performance.}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} Somebody who behaves or reacts in an admirably good-natured manner, e.g. to being teased or to losing a game; a [[good sport]].
#: {{ux|en|You're such a '''sport'''! You never get upset when we tease you.}}
# {{lb|en|archaic}} Something fun, [[pastime]]; [[amusement]].
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 6-2|III|ii|passage=Think it but a minute spent in '''sport'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Sidney Arcadia|21|283|Her '''sports''' were such as carried riches of knowledge upon the stream of delight.}}
#: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:hobby}}
# {{lb|en|archaic}} Mockery, making fun; derision.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merry Wives|act=III|scene=iii|page=58|column=2|passage=Why then make '''ſport''' at me, then let me be your ieſt}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} A toy; a plaything; an object of mockery.
#* {{RQ:Dryden Aeneis|6|passage=flitting leaves, the '''sport''' of every wind}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=a. 1676|author=John Clarke|title=On Governing the Temper
|passage=Never does man appear to greater disadvantage than when he is the '''sport''' of his own ungoverned passions.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} Gaming for money as in racing, hunting{{,}} or fishing.
# {{lb|en|biology|botany|zoology|countable}} A plant or an animal, or part of a plant or animal, which has some peculiarity not usually seen in the species; an abnormal variety or growth. The term encompasses both [[mutant]]s and organisms with non-genetic developmental abnormalities such as [[birth defect]]s.
#* {{RQ:Haggard She|passage=We never shot another like it, so I do not know if it was a `'''sport'''' or a distinct species.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|author=Charles Quest-Ritson| title=The Dutch garden where tulip bulbs live forever: Hortus Bulborum, a volunteer-run Dutch garden, is dedicated to conserving historic varieties before they vanish for good [print version: Inspired by a living bulb archive, 27 September 2014, p. G5]| url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/gardening/gardenstovisit/11121226/The-Dutch-garden-where-tulip-bulbs-live-forever.html| work={{w|The Daily Telegraph}} (Gardening)| date=26 September 2014| passage=At Hortus Bulborum you will find heirloom narcissi that date back at least to the 15th century and famous old tulips like 'Duc van Tol' (1595) and its '''sports'''.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251001122203/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/gardening/gardenstovisit/11121226/The-Dutch-garden-where-tulip-bulbs-live-forever.html|archivedate=1 October 2025}}
# {{lb|en|slang|countable}} A [[sportsman]]; a gambler.
# {{lb|en|slang|countable}} One who consorts with disreputable people, including prostitutes.
# {{lb|en|obsolete|uncountable}} An amorous [[dalliance]].
# {{lb|en|informal|usually singular}} A [[friend]] or [[acquaintance]] ''(chiefly used when speaking to the friend in question)''
#: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:friend}}
# {{non-gloss|Term of endearment used by an adult for a child, usually a boy}}.
#: {{ux|en|Hey, '''sport'''! You've gotten so big since I saw you last! Give me five.}}
# {{lb|en|archaic}} Play; idle jingle.
#* '''1725-1726''', {{w|William Broome}}, ''The Odyssey''
#*: An author who should introduce such a '''sport''' of words upon our stage {{...}}would meet with small applause.

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To amuse oneself, to [[play]].
#: {{ux|en|children '''sporting''' on the green}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To mock or tease, treat lightly, toy with.
#: {{ux|en|Jen '''sports''' with Bill's emotions.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1663|author=w:John Tillotson|title=The Wisdom of being Religious
|passage=He '''sports''' with his own life.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[display]]; to have as a notable [[feature]].
#: {{syn|en|rock|wear}}
#: {{ux|en|Jen's '''sporting''' a new pair of shoes;  he was '''sporting''' a new wound from the combat}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-07-20|volume=408|issue=8845| title=[http://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21581981-what-pollution-some-opportunity-others-welcome-plastisphere Welcome to the plastisphere]| passage=[The researchers] noticed many of their pieces of [plastic marine] debris '''sported''' surface pits around two microns across. Such pits are about the size of a bacterial cell. Closer examination showed that some of these pits did, indeed, contain bacteria, […].}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|date=2023-06-03|author=w:Carl Zimmer|title=How Did Birds First Take Off?|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/06/03/science/bird-flight-evolution.html|passage=He was especially happy to see one of the most important discoveries make it to the screen: dinosaurs that '''sported''' feathers. But judging from the emails he has been receiving, some moviegoers did not share his excitement.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250828181404/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/06/03/science/bird-flight-evolution.html|archivedate=28 August 2025}}
# {{lb|en|reflexive}} To [[divert]]; to [[amuse]]; to [[make merry]].
#* {{RQ:KJV|Isaiah|57|4|passage=Against whom do ye '''sport''' yourselves?}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To represent by any kind of play.
#* {{RQ:Dryden Juvenal Satires|6|passage=Now '''sporting''' on thy lyre the loves of youth.}}
# To practise the diversions of the field or the turf; to be given to betting, as upon races.
# To assume suddenly a new and different character from the rest of the [[plant]] or from the type of the [[species]]; said of a bud, shoot, plant, or animal.
#* {{RQ:Darwin Variation|passage=more than one kind of rose has '''sported''' into a moss}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|archaic}} To [[close#Verb|close]] (a [[door#Noun|door]]).
